questions.subject: CALCULUS_I
questions.topic: related rates setup - ladder with wall, 5-12-13 triple
questions.learningObjective: Model a constant-length geometric constraint with time derivatives and solve for an unknown rate
questions.stem: A 13 ft ladder leans against a wall. The foot of the ladder is pulled away from the wall at 2 ft/s. How fast is the top of the ladder sliding DOWN the wall (ft/s) when the foot is 5 ft from the wall?
questions.explanation: Because the ladder length is fixed, x^2 + y^2 = 169 holds at every instant. Implicit differentiation with respect to t gives 2x(dx/dt) + 2y(dy/dt) = 0, so dy/dt = -x(dx/dt)/y. At x=5 the 5-12-13 triple gives y=12, hence dy/dt = -(5)(2)/12 = -5/6 ft/s; the negative sign means the height decreases.
questions.hint: Write the constant-length relation first, then differentiate every variable with respect to t.

questions.subject: CALCULUS_I
questions.topic: related rates setup - circular ripple area
questions.learningObjective: Differentiate A = pi r^2 with respect to time and solve for dr/dt
questions.stem: A dropped stone creates an expanding circular ripple whose area grows at 75 cm^2/s. How fast is the radius increasing (cm/s) when the radius is 5 cm?
questions.explanation: Area and radius are both functions of t, so A = pi r^2 becomes dA/dt = 2 pi r dr/dt. Substituting dA/dt = 75 and r = 5 gives 75 = 10 pi dr/dt, hence dr/dt = 75/(10 pi) = 7.5/pi, about 2.39 cm/s. Radius growth slows over time because the same area gain spreads over a larger circumference.
questions.hint: Differentiate A = pi r^2 with respect to t, not r.

questions.subject: CALCULUS_I
questions.topic: related rates computation - inflating spherical balloon volume

questions.stem: Air is pumped into a spherical balloon at 288 pi cm^3/min. How fast is the radius increasing (cm/min) when the diameter is 12 cm?
questions.explanation: The chain rule applied to V = (4/3) pi r^3 gives dV/dt = 4 pi r^2 dr/dt. Diameter 12 means r = 6, so 288 pi = 4 pi (36) dr/dt = 144 pi dr/dt and dr/dt = 2 cm/min. The answer is independent of pi because it appears on both sides of the equation.
questions.hint: Use dV/dt = 4 pi r^2 dr/dt and solve for the radius rate.

questions.subject: CALCULUS_I
questions.topic: related rates computation - plane flying toward observer

questions.stem: A plane flies level at 3 mi altitude and passes directly over an observer at 400 mph. How fast is the distance between plane and observer increasing (mph) one minute after the plane passes overhead?
questions.explanation: With x the horizontal distance past the observer and z the slant distance, x^2 + 9 = z^2. Differentiating gives 2x(dx/dt) = 2z(dz/dt), so dz/dt = x(dx/dt)/z. One minute at 400 mph is x = 20/3 mi, giving z = sqrt(481)/3, and dz/dt = 8000/sqrt(481), about 364.8 mph. As the plane recedes the slant range approaches the ground speed.
questions.hint: Convert one minute of travel to horizontal distance before differentiating.

questions.stem: An inverted cone (vertex down, radius 4 m, height 16 m) is filled with water at 2 m^3/min. How fast is the water level rising (m/min) when the water depth is 8 m?
questions.explanation: By similar triangles the water radius is r = h/4, so V = (1/3) pi r^2 h = pi h^3/48 and dV/dt = (pi h^2/16) dh/dt. Setting 2 = (pi 64/16) dh/dt gives dh/dt = 32/(64 pi) = 1/(2 pi), about 0.159 m/min.
questions.hint: Use similar triangles to write r in terms of h before differentiating.

questions.subject: CALCULUS_I
questions.topic: related rates computation - moving shadow tip
questions.learningObjective: Set up a similar-triangle relation between object distance and shadow length and differentiate
questions.stem: A 6 ft tall man walks away from a 15 ft lamppost at 5 ft/s. At what speed does the tip of his shadow move along the ground (ft/s) when he is 10 ft from the base of the post?
questions.explanation: Similar triangles give 15/(x+s) = 6/s, where x is his distance from the post and s his shadow length, so 9s = 6x and s = (2/3)x. The tip sits at x + s = (5/3)x from the post, and differentiating gives d/dt(x+s) = (5/3) dx/dt = 25/3, about 8.33 ft/s. The current distance 10 ft drops out because the relation is linear.
questions.hint: The tip distance is x + s, not s alone.

questions.stem: An observer stands 100 ft from a launch pad. The angle of elevation of a rocket is increasing at 0.05 rad/s. How fast (ft/s) is the rocket rising when the angle is 45 degrees?
questions.explanation: Let y be the altitude. Since tan(theta) = y/100, differentiating gives sec^2(theta) d(theta)/dt = (1/100) dy/dt. At theta = 45 degrees sec^2(theta) = 2, so dy/dt = 100(2)(0.05) = 10 ft/s. The sec^2 factor is the reason angle growth does not translate into a constant height rate.

questions.stem: A rectangle's length is 20 cm growing at 3 cm/s and its width is 10 cm shrinking at 2 cm/s. How fast is the length of its diagonal changing (cm/s)?
questions.explanation: The diagonal satisfies d^2 = l^2 + w^2, so 2d dd/dt = 2l dl/dt + 2w dw/dt and dd/dt = (l dl/dt + w dw/dt)/d. Here d = sqrt(500) = 22.36 and the numerator is 20(3) + 10(-2) = 40, giving dd/dt = 40/sqrt(500), about 1.789 cm/s. Each side contributes proportionally to its length.
